title: replay-window-contraction-and-scheduler-integrity-guard
author: Alyssa Chen
release_notes: Introduces adaptive replay-window contraction and a scheduler integrity guard to reduce cudagraph warmup flaps across variable-prefix workloads; adds KV-cache tiling alignment for stable kernel selection; safe rollout behind feature flag.
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent cudagraph warmup regressions when serving mixed-prefix workloads (wide variance in prefix lengths and KV cache tiling). Captures would occasionally pick kernels that later proved incompatible with longer/shorter prefix permutations causing immediate replay failures or a cascade of fallbacks that amplified latency spikes. This PR implements a defensive, adaptive approach to reduce warmup flaps while preserving the latency wins of cudagraphs.

What this PR does (single-pass overview):
- Adaptive replay-window contraction: the replay manager now tracks a time-weighted history of successful captures keyed by (model, device_arch, kv_tiling, prefix_bucket). When shape variance within a bucket exceeds a threshold we conservatively contract the replay window for that bucket (i.e., reduce the number of replayed iterations and increase probe frequency) to avoid committing to an unstable capture.
- Scheduler integrity guard: a lightweight verification layer in the scheduler verifies kernel / convolution selection stability before a captured graph is promoted to long-lived use. If the guard detects a mismatch during priming, we trigger a controlled backoff (temporary non-cudagraph path) and schedule a probing capture instead of immediate promotion.
- KV-cache tiling alignment: continuous-batching and KV cache placement can skew memory layouts causing kernel-compatibility differences at capture time. We introduce a tiler that aligns KV-cache layout heuristically at capture time and tags the capture with the tiling signature so replays are matched only when layout-compatible.
- Backoff & graceful fallback: instead of immediate wide rollback, the runtime now performs exponential backoff of replay promotion and falls back to the non-graph path for a fixed number of iterations to allow the workload to stabilize. The backoff is jittered to minimize synchronized retries across workers.
- Observability and instrumentation: new telemetry metrics (cudagraph.replay_backoff.count, cudagraph.replay_promotion_latency_ms, cudagraph.kv_tiling.mismatch_count) and logging traces for captures/promotions. Added debug-only histograms that helped diagnose the original regressions in perf lab runs.
- Feature gating and rollout: the entire new logic is gated behind the runtime feature-flag "replay_adaptive_guard_v2" and defaults to off for Dedicated customers. Admins can opt in per-deployment and per-model.

Design notes / rationale:
- We intentionally avoid altering kernel-selection heuristics; instead we add a safety layer that verifies kernel stability across short-term shape variance. Changing kernel heuristics directly proved brittle in previous experiments and caused regression blasts when run across heterogeneous GPUs.
- The replay-window contraction is tuned to prefer shorter, fast-probing windows on high-variance buckets (interactive workloads with many short prefixes) and wider windows for stable, long-sequence workloads. This keeps throughput benefits where safe and reduces warmup regressions where not.

Performance & validation (summary):
- Perf-lab synthetic mixed-prefix test (80% short prefixes <64 tokens, 20% long prefixes >512 tokens): warmup failure rate before fix: ~9.8% (cudagraph replays that fallback at least once per 1k captures); after fix: ~2.1% (78% reduction). Measured with 8xA100 pool.
- Tail latency (p95) on the synthetic trace improved by ~7% during steady-state due to more stable graph promotions; transient p99 spikes decreased by ~42% because fewer fallback cascades occurred.
- Microbenchmarks show a 1.5%-2.3% overhead for the integrity guard checks in priming path (amortized away for promoted graphs). We added configuration knobs to disable aggressive checks if ultra-low overhead path is required.

Commits (high-level):
- Add adaptive replay window state machine and persistence layer
- Introduce scheduler integrity guard & promotion policy
- Implement kv_cache tiler and tiling-signature matching
- Add telemetry metrics + dashboards and unit/integration tests
- Add feature flag and rollout script + docs

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Morales (requested changes, 2025-08-24): "Please add a deterministic unit test that simulates two workers racing on promotion and verify the jitter/backoff avoids thundering-herd promotions. Also add a comment explaining why we don't bake tiling into kernel selection heuristics." 
  - Author reply (2025-08-25): "Added scheduler_guard_race_test in tests/unit and expanded comments in integrity_guard.h. Race test uses deterministic fake clock and verifies backoff windows across 3 workers." 
- Priya Nair (performance review, 2025-08-27): "Can you share the perf-lab config and raw histograms? Need to validate across 4xV100 and 8xA100 configs before approval." 
  - Author reply (2025-08-28): "Attached perf lab job ids and added dashboards link in the PR description. Verified histograms for both configs; summary included above." 
- Ethan Zhang (observability, 2025-08-29): "Add a tag to traces to correlate replay promotion attempts with kv_tiling signatures and include a severity for repeated mismatches so ops can alert." 
  - Author reply (2025-08-30): "Added cudagraph.kv_tiling.signature tag to traces and a severity label on mismatch metric. Updated dashboard panels and added alert runbook references in docs/runtime/replay_adaptive_guard_v2.md." 
- Final approval from Priya and Diego (2025-09-01) after small nits fixed.

CI notes:
- Initial CI run (2025-08-26) failed two flaky integration tests; rerun and fixed a timing dependency in tests/integration/cudagraph_replay_variance.test.cpp. Final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main gated off by default.
2) Canary rollout to perf-canary cluster for 48 hours with 5% traffic. Monitor new metrics and p99 regressions.
3) Gradual increase to 25% then 100% for non-Dedicated customers. Dedicated customers are opt-in.
4) If mismatch_count or replay_backoff.count increases by >3x baseline, automatic rollback hook will disable the feature flag cluster-wide.

Testing & QA:
- Added deterministic unit tests covering promotion backoff, tiling signature matching, and scheduler guard race conditions.
- Integration tests in perf-lab ran synthetic mixed-prefix traces with multiple GPU configurations.
- Local stress harness validated jittered backoff reduces synchronized promotions across 16 worker processes.

Migration notes:
- No customer-facing API changes. Config default remains off. Admins who opted in previously will see new metrics and must ensure feature flag is set to true for both runtime and console rollout.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Investigate optional safe encoding of tiling signatures in model metadata so capture/replay matching can happen across model version pinning events.
- Explore light-weight kernel-selection feedback loop that uses promotion history to recommend per-model capture targets (separate PR).

Summary: This change reduces cudagraph warmup flaps for mixed-prefix workloads by combining an adaptive replay-window with a scheduler integrity guard and KV-cache tiling alignment. It is conservative by default, observable, and opt-in for Dedicated customers. Merged to main via squash on 2025-09-02.
